name: MimicPlay
summary: MimicPlay splits the problem by level. A high-level latent planner is learned from unstructured human play video — cheap, no robot, no action labels — to predict future hand trajectories, and a low-level policy conditioned on those plans is learned from a small number of robot teleoperation demonstrations. The split matches where each data source is actually strong: humans supply what to do next, the robot supplies how to do it.
innovation: Assigns human video to the planning level and robot data to the control level, so the embodiment gap only has to be crossed once, coarsely.
Latent plans over future hand trajectories as the interface between the two levels.
matters: An influential template for the human/robot data division of labour that hierarchical VLAs later adopted.
limits: Hand-trajectory plans carry no force or fine contact information, so precision tasks stay with the robot data.
lineage: WHIRL's human prior formalized as a learned high-level planner sitting over a robot low-level policy.
